summary: Cantoni's conjecture (1950) — that every planar cubic graph with exactly three Hamilton cycles contains a triangle — remains open as far as can be determined. An arXiv full-text search returned no papers addressing it by name, the Open Problem Garden has no dedicated entry, and every fetched paper on planar cubic Hamilton cycles either addressed unrelated variants or mentioned only graphs with four or more Hamilton cycles. The conjecture is thematically close to Vizing's (1965) open question on uniquely 3-edge-colorable cubic planar graphs having a triangle; the connection is that a uniquely 3-edge-colorable cubic graph has exactly three Hamilton cycles, so Vizing's question is a special case. Ninčák (1974) and Tutte (1976) are cited in Bondy–Murty as related works, but their specific contributions to the conjecture could not be verified from available online sources.

The conjecture is distinct from but related to Vizing's (1965) conjecture (uniquely 3-edge-colorable cubic graphs have a triangle), since unique 3-edge-colorability implies exactly three Hamilton cycles; the converse need not hold, so Cantoni's conjecture is potentially weaker. Bondy–Murty cross-references Ninčák (1974) and Tutte (1976); these 1970s papers likely contain partial results or reformulations but could not be fetched.
